chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلٍ يُزَوِّجُ مَمْلُوكًا لَهُ امْرَأَةً حُرَّةً عَلَى مِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ بَاعَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهَا

translations.en: Regarding a man who marries his slave to a free woman for one hundred dirhams, then sells him before he consummates the marriage with her,

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ: «يُعْطِيهَا سَيِّدُهُ مِنْ ثَمَنِهِ نِصْفَ مَا فَرَضَ لَهَا إِنَّمَا هُوَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ دَيْنٍ اسْتَدَانَهُ بِإِذْنِ سَيِّدِهِ».

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "Her master gives her, from his sale-price, half of what was assigned to her. It is only in the position of a debt that he incurred with the permission of his master."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the marriage of a male slave to a free woman when a dowry has been set and the slave is sold before consummation. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the woman is entitled to half of the specified dowry, paid from the slave's sale-price, because the dowry obligation is treated like a debt incurred with the master's permission.
en.seo_question: If a master marries his slave to a free woman and then sells him before consummation, who must pay the dowry?

key_terms.مَمْلُوكًا: a male slave owned by the master
key_terms.حُرَّةً: a free woman, not a bondwoman
key_terms.مِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: the specified dowry amount of one hundred dirhams
key_terms.ثَمَنِهِ: the price received from selling the slave
key_terms.نِصْفَ: half, indicating half of the specified dowry is due
key_terms.فَرَضَ: stipulated or assigned as the dowry obligation
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ: with the permission or authorization of the master
